selected_mechanism.name: The Anchorage utility capacity statement: AO 2026-27 / AMC Title 21 data center conditional-use gate
selected_mechanism.one_line_definition: Anchorage made data centers (defined as 20 MW or more at peak) a conditional use in industrial districts only, and made a written system-capacity statement from the serving electrical utility a mandatory component of the permit application, delegating the binding siting determination to a non-municipal member-owned cooperative that sits upstream of any public hearing.

news_trigger.what_happened: “The larger it gets, the more detailed the analysis gets,” he explained. “That would determine if we have the ability to serve it or not.”
news_trigger.speaker: Nathan Minnema, Chief Operating Officer, Golden Valley Electric Association
news_trigger.corroborating_quote: “We have a way of saying, ‘Does this work for the community or does it not?’” Klouda said. “I think that having that kind of framework in place is really important.”

layers.name: L1 - Use classification (the Assembly's enabling act)
layers.what_it_does: Amends AMC Title 21 to make data centers a conditional use in the I-1 light industrial, I-2 heavy industrial and I-3 rural industrial districts, and no residential district, while waiving Planning and Zoning Commission review of the ordinance itself.
layers.controlling_actor: Anchorage Assembly (adopted 2026-03-27, 10-2; introduced by Assembly Vice Chair Brawley and Assembly Member Volland)
layers.verbatim_anchor: “18. Data centers.” listed under I-1 conditional uses; “11. Data centers.” under I-2; title reads “...AND WAIVING PLANNING AND ZONING COMMISSION REVIEW.”

layers.name: L2 - Definition and threshold (who is captured)
layers.what_it_does: Sets the jurisdictional trigger at 20 MW and splits small/large at 2,000 servers; imposes a 200-foot setback from residential or noise-sensitive uses, waivable by the Director only for small data centers; aggregates geographically dispersed infrastructure under common ownership into a single facility.
layers.controlling_actor: Planning Department Director (holds the setback waiver and the mechanical-feasibility determination on equipment enclosure)
layers.verbatim_anchor: “Data Center means facility or co-located facilities that house computer servers for processing and storing data and requires at least 20 megawatts of electrical demand at peak operation.” / “The Director may waive this requirement only for small data centers.”

layers.name: L3 - Electrical utility written statement (THE CHOKEPOINT)
layers.what_it_does: Makes a written statement from the serving electrical utility, demonstrating sufficient system capacity at peak demand, a mandatory component of the conditional use application whenever the facility connects to the grid. The ordinance provides no rebuttal path for a withheld or negative statement.
layers.controlling_actor: The serving electrical utility. In the Anchorage Bowl, Chugach Electric Association, an independent member-owned cooperative, not a municipal department

secondary_source_for_actor_identity.verbatim_anchor: “Chugach is the largest member-owned electric cooperative in Alaska”; service territory “extends from Anchorage to the northern Kenai Peninsula”

layers.verbatim_anchor: “If the facility requires connecting to and drawing power from the surrounding electrical grid, the application must include a written statement from the electrical utility or utilities demonstrating that there is sufficient system capacity to meet the facility’s projected demand at peak operation.”

layers.name: L4 - Wastewater utility statement and codified burden shift
layers.what_it_does: Requires a written statement from the wastewater utility on sewer capacity, and expressly empowers that utility to state that the discharge is likely to cause significant adverse impacts, which creates a presumption that an approval criterion is NOT met, overcome only by clear and convincing evidence before the commission.
layers.controlling_actor: The serving wastewater utility (as named in the ordinance text)
layers.source_caveat: AS-INTRODUCED TEXT ONLY, NOT CORROBORATED POST-ENACTMENT. Supporting color only. The writer must lead with L3.
layers.verbatim_anchor: “Such a statement by the wastewater utility creates a presumption that the approval criterion at 21.03.080D.7 is not met. This presumption may only be overcome by clear and convincing evidence presented to the commission.”

layers.name: L5 - Conditional use adjudication
layers.what_it_does: Hears the conditional use application and grants or denies it; may impose additional screening through the review. Requires a supermajority in effect: five affirmative votes regardless of how many commissioners are seated.
layers.controlling_actor: Anchorage Planning and Zoning Commission, nine citizens appointed by the Mayor

primary_source.outlet: Municipality of Anchorage, Office of Community Planning and Development

layers.verbatim_anchor: “No matter how many Commissioners are present it takes 5 yes votes to approve the conditional use permit.”

layers.name: L6 - State water appropriation (the off-grid path)
layers.what_it_does: Where a facility uses onsite water rather than the public system, cooling water becomes a state water-rights question: a significant appropriation requires a DNR permit, and appropriations above 5,000 gpd trigger public notice.
layers.controlling_actor: ADNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Water Resources Section
layers.verbatim_anchor: “Public notice is required if the appropriation is greater than 5,000 gpd.”

layers.name: L7 - Appeal
layers.what_it_does: A denial is appealed by filing a notice of appeal with the Municipal Clerk, which sends the Commission's action to the Board of Adjustment for review.
layers.controlling_actor: Municipality of Anchorage Board of Adjustment (via the Municipal Clerk)

primary_source.outlet: Municipality of Anchorage, Office of Community Planning and Development

layers.verbatim_anchor: “File a notice of appeal with the Municipal Clerk’s office to have the Planning and Zoning Commission’s action reviewed by the Board of Adjustment.”
layers.scout_claims_dropped: The scouts' 20-day appeal clock and the 'strict legal review, not a re-hearing' standard do NOT appear on the fetched page and are excluded rather than asserted.

chokepoint.actor: The serving electrical utility as an institutional role. In the Anchorage Bowl, Chugach Electric Association, an independent member-owned cooperative
chokepoint.binary_decision: Issue, or withhold, a written statement demonstrating sufficient system capacity to meet the facility's projected demand at peak operation.
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: It is a mandatory application component, not an approval criterion weighed in the balance: no statement, no complete application, no hearing. It sits entirely upstream of the visible five-vote Planning and Zoning hearing. It is held by a single non-municipal, unelected cooperative that no municipal body can override. It carries no published timeline. And decisively, the ordinance drafters knew how to write a rebuttal path when they wanted one, giving the wastewater presumption an express clear-and-convincing escape, but gave the electrical statement none at all.

ak_consequence.sector: Data center and AI compute siting, and the utilities that serve it
ak_consequence.decision_or_risk: Any grid-connected data center of 20 MW or more proposed in Anchorage must obtain a written system-capacity statement from Chugach Electric Association before its conditional use application is even complete, a determination with no published timeline, no municipal override, and no rebuttal path in the code.
ak_consequence.named_actor: Chugach Electric Association (Anchorage); Golden Valley Electric Association plays the equivalent role in the Fairbanks template
ak_consequence.timeframe: In force now. The ordinance took effect on passage 2026-03-27; Mat-Su Borough still has no data-center regulation and FNSB's comprehensive plan is in draft, with the 2026-08-27 Alaska Municipal League conference in Fairbanks positioning Anchorage's ordinance as the statewide template.

selected_mechanism.structural_read: Anchorage built the gate before the applicants arrived, and in doing so it did something more consequential than zoning: it converted a private interconnection study into a precondition for a public land-use approval. The politically visible layer is the five-vote Planning and Zoning hearing, which is a committee and therefore not where leverage lives. The leverage lives in a load study performed by a member-owned cooperative that answers to its ratepayers, not to the Assembly, on no clock. The ordinance also writes its own escape: every utility-statement requirement is conditioned on connecting to the grid, the public water system, or the public sewer. A facility that generates behind the meter and runs closed-loop water triggers none of them. Anchorage has thus priced grid-connected compute and left off-grid compute comparatively unpriced, which is precisely the configuration the live Alaska proposals already favor. The binding constraint on Alaska compute is not zoning. It is interconnection, and the utility owns it.

forward_implication.next_decision_point: Model the grid-connect path against the behind-the-meter path explicitly for any Alaska compute siting decision, and treat the utility capacity statement, not the zoning hearing, as the schedule-driving milestone. For anyone drafting in Mat-Su or FNSB off the Anchorage template, the question to raise now is whether a withheld electrical statement gets any rebuttal path at all, since Anchorage gave one to wastewater and none to power.
forward_implication.date_or_window: This week, while FNSB's comprehensive plan is still in draft and Mat-Su has no data-center rule on the books. The AML conference of 2026-08-27 opened the copying window.
forward_implication.who_is_positioned: Developers with captive or behind-the-meter generation are positioned to bypass the chokepoint entirely; grid-dependent hyperscale entrants into Anchorage are exposed to an untimed Chugach load study with no appeal.

finalists: Candidate A - Anchorage data center conditional-use gate
overlap_rule_applied.resolution: Chokepoint asymmetry decided it. Both nominal chokepoints are single-actor, but asymmetry must be documented, not asserted. Candidate B's single-officer authority appears only in secondary law-firm text; SBA Policy Notice 6000-876995 was unreachable and 13 CFR 124.112 and 124.503 name no individual official, only 'SBA'. Candidate A's chokepoint is in primary code text. A wins.
overlap_rule_applied.category_choice: The facilities framing locates leverage at the utility capacity statement; the regulatory framing locates it at the five-vote P&Z hearing, which is a committee and explicitly disqualified as a chokepoint. Leverage decides, so FACILITIES.

_validation_note: REVERSAL ON RE-RUN, RECORDED IN FULL. The mapper's first pass returned no_target and dropped Candidate A on the ground that no source identified who makes the capacity determination. That was an ENVIRONMENTAL failure, not an evidentiary one: this container lacked poppler-utils, so AO 2026-27.pdf rendered as binary and the mapper fell back on a Davis Wright Tremaine analysis stating 'The text does not explicitly identify which entity makes the capacity determination.' The orchestrator installed poppler-utils and extracted the ordinance; it says it outright. The mapper then independently re-read the raw pdftotext output and confirmed each quote at its line number rather than trusting the orchestrator's evidence pack. VERSION CAVEAT: the recovered PDF header reads 'For reading: February 17, 2026' with a blank PASSED AND APPROVED block, so this is the AS-INTRODUCED text; enactment was 2026-03-27, 10-2. library.municode.com 403'd on two retries, so the codified enacted text could not be read. Post-enactment DWT independently corroborates the three provisions that carry the mechanism (20 MW threshold, 200-foot setback, capacity-demonstration requirement), so the chokepoint is double-sourced across introduced text and post-enactment analysis. The L4 wastewater clear-and-convincing burden flip rests on as-introduced text ALONE and is NOT corroborated; it is supporting color and the writer must lead with the L3 electrical statement. That single-sourcing is why confidence is medium rather than high. Further honesty notes: awwu.biz 403'd, so the identity and municipal status of Anchorage's wastewater utility was NOT verified and L4's actor is named only as 'the wastewater utility' exactly as the ordinance does; and the scouts' 20-day appeal clock and 'strict legal review' standard were dropped rather than asserted. Window used 14 days for the selected mechanism (trigger 1 day old); Candidate B was evaluated under the 21-day outer allowance and still failed.
